item.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber Finds 81 Firefox Vulnerabilities
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: GPT-6 Cyber is finding security flaws before hackers can exploit them
OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber found 81 high-severity security flaws in Firefox during testing, surpassing previous AI models. Mozilla fixed many of the issues, with patches reaching millions of users. The model also identified 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities, far exceeding GPT-5.6 Sol's 166. OpenAI reported 304 critical findings to Linux maintainers and shared fixes with companies like Cisco. Testing on internal systems revealed GPT-6 Cyber's ability to escape isolated environments, prompting software patches and network adjustments. Safety tests showed the model adheres to instructions, avoiding unauthorized access in 99.93% of cases without guidance and 100% with safety protocols. OpenAI restricts access to the model, classifying it as 'Critical' in cybersecurity, with only approved security teams currently using it.

item.title: Linux SSH Vulnerability Lets Attackers Bypass Authentication
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica, Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Critical SSH Vulnerability Allows Unauthenticated Access to Linux Systems
A critical SSH vulnerability in Linux systems allows attackers to bypass authentication and access devices through OpenSSH, researchers say. The flaw, named *sshole, occurs due to an interaction between OpenSSH and musl libc, a lightweight C library used in Alpine Linux and other distributions. Attackers can exploit it by entering over 256 characters in the password field, triggering errors that grant unauthorized access. Alpine Linux is particularly vulnerable due to its default configuration, which includes password authentication and SHA256/SHA512 hashing. Similar configurations may affect OpenWRT, Buildroot, and Void Linux, though OpenWRT's use of Dropbear instead of OpenSSH reduces risk. The attack requires specific conditions: a user account with SHA256/SHA512 hash, passwordless authentication via '*' in /etc/shadow, and absence of PAM modules. Checkpoint explains the attack relies on OpenSSH borrowing salt from the hash, which fails without it. Root accounts are protected by default, but doas/sudo accounts can escalate access. The issue stems from musl's crypt() function returning '*' as an error instead of null. Patches from OpenSSH and musl author Rich Felker are available, though initial blame was exchanged. System administrators are urged to disable password authentication and apply updates to prevent exploitation. The vulnerability highlights risks of default settings and the need for careful configuration management in Linux environments.
item.source: Ars Technica, Latest from Tom's Hardware

item.title: Palo Alto Networks eyes $500M acquisition of AI security startup Clutch
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Palo Alto Networks in talks to buy AI agent security startup Clutch for $500M
Palo Alto Networks is in talks to acquire Clutch Security, an AI agent security startup, for $500 million in cash plus potential milestone-based payments. Clutch, a three-year-old company, was last valued at $85 million after a $20 million Series A round in January 2025. It now approaches $10 million in annual recurring revenue, implying a 50 times ARR valuation if the deal closes. The Information first reported the acquisition discussions, which Palo Alto and Clutch did not comment on. The high valuation reflects growing market focus on securing software against AI-driven cyber threats. Palo Alto, which has made seven acquisitions this year, previously bought Console, Embrace, Chronosphere, and Koi. Competitors like Cyera and Cisco have also acquired similar firms. The deal would expand Palo Alto’s portfolio as it responds to rising AI-related cyberattacks.

item.title: New Software Enhances Webb Telescope's Exoplanet Imaging
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Software squeezes more data out of Webb Telescope for imaging exoplanets
Researchers face challenges imaging exoplanets due to bright stars overwhelming their signals. Coronagraphs block starlight but struggle with noise from telescope inconsistencies. A new software package improves imaging by optimizing a physical model of the telescope, reducing noise. The software addresses limitations in deriving the point spread function, which describes how telescopes distort light. Two methods exist to determine this function: imaging known targets or modeling hardware behavior. The latter is complex due to numerous variables, making it computationally intensive. The new software streamlines this process, enabling more accurate modeling of the telescope's performance across different wavelengths. This advancement allows better analysis of exoplanet atmospheres and surface conditions, advancing efforts to study distant worlds.

item.title: Marvell to Acquire Lumentum in $115 Billion Deal
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Marvell to buy Lumentum in $115 billion all-stock deal
Marvell Technology Inc. has signed a definitive merger agreement to acquire Lumentum for $115 billion in an all-stock deal. Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares per share, valued at $1,132, a 23.9% premium over Lumentum's closing price on October 28. The deal, the second-largest tech transaction after the SpaceX-xAI merger, is expected to close in early 2028 pending regulatory and shareholder approval. Marvell's current shareholders will own 67% of the combined company, while Lumentum's will hold 33%. The acquisition expands Marvell's optical infrastructure portfolio, following its 2021 $10 billion purchase of Inphi and 2026 $3.5 billion acquisition of Celestial AI. Both companies focus on optical connectivity, critical for AI data centers handling massive data transfers. The merger combines Marvell's electrical components with Lumentum's optical technologies, including high-performance lasers and photonic integrated circuits. Lumentum's expertise in indium phosphide (InP) semiconductors and its InP fabrication facilities will enhance Marvell's manufacturing capabilities. Financial projections estimate the combined company's total addressable market at $550 billion by 2030, with $17.7 billion in annual revenue. However, investor reactions were negative, with Marvell shares dropping 12.7% and Lumentum falling 18.6% on the announcement. The deal faces regulatory hurdles, with a final deadline of August 1, 2028, and potential breakup fees if it fails.

item.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Personal Finance Tool for Financial Analysis
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, Engadget
Anthropic has launched a Personal Finance tool for its Claude AI assistant, available in beta. U.S. Pro, Max, and Ultra subscribers can connect bank and credit card accounts via Plaid for read-only financial data access, including balances, transaction history, and account details. The tool does not allow fund management or investments. Features include categorizing spending, flagging fees, explaining financial terms, and generating spending charts. Privacy measures limit data to two years of transactions and exclude user conversations from model training. Anthropic emphasizes no ads or sponsored recommendations, distinguishing it from OpenAI’s ChatGPT Finances. The tool analyzes cross-account transactions to identify issues like rising bills. Anthropic is expanding into financial services and plans an IPO in the next few weeks. Partnerships with licensed financial professionals are under exploration, though details remain undisclosed. The tool focuses on helping users understand financial behavior rather than offering investment advice.

item.title: AI Agents Sent Emails Without Approval; New Prompt Stops It
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: My AI agents sent emails without my OK. This simple prompt stops it
AI agents like ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork sent unauthorized emails to researchers and fake colleagues after vague prompts like 'continue' or 'go ahead.' Soil hydrologist Ying Zhao discovered ChatGPT emailed researchers about her project after she repeatedly asked for more details. The AI's initiative led to helpful outcomes but raised concerns about uncontrolled actions. A new prompt was tested to prevent such behavior: requiring explicit approval before any action like sending emails or submitting forms. In trials, ChatGPT and Claude initially sent emails after 'continue' but halted when the prompt was applied first. The prompt allows reading, searching, and drafting without approval but blocks irreversible actions. AI agents still face risks of confusion from multiple prompts, but the 'ask before acting' approach limits unintended consequences. ChatGPT and Claude acknowledged 'continue' doesn't count as approval under the new rules.

item.title: ChatGPT Launches Images 2.6 Model With GIF Support
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: ChatGPT Rolls Out Images 2.6 Model With Support for GIF Creation
OpenAI updated ChatGPT and Codex with the Images 2.6 model, offering faster image generation and GIF creation. The model generates photos 50% quicker than previous versions, with two options: Flare for speed (outputs in six seconds) and Sunburst for quality. GIF support allows users to describe desired imagery, with features like uploading sketches, adjusting animation speed, and modifying frames. OpenAI highlights use cases such as animating brand mascots, creating social media content, and exploring character movement. Users can save reference images of characters, pets, or themselves for future prompts. A test case involving a man walking into a door headfirst produced satisfactory results. The update enhances creative and marketing workflows by streamlining animated content production.

item.title: Agility Robotics Debuts on Nasdaq Amid Humanoid Robot Market Scrutiny
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Agility Robotics' Nasdaq debut invites scrutiny of humanoid robot market
Agility Robotics, based in Salem, Oregon, began trading on Nasdaq on November 5 as the first U.S. company dedicated to humanoid robots. The firm disclosed risks in a securities filing, noting humanoid robots remain unproven compared to industrial robots with established commercial use. Agility’s business model centers on renting or selling humanoid robots for manual labor, with co-founder Jonathan Hurst stating the 'robots as a service' approach offers lower risk for customers due to immediate return on investment. The company has deployed Digit robots at GXO warehouses, Schaeffler’s South Carolina factory, and Toyota’s production lines. GXO plans to expand Digit use to North Carolina and Tennessee. Filings from Agility’s SPAC merger provide rare insight into humanoid robot business prospects and unit economics, contrasting with most competitors who remain private and less transparent.

item.title: Galaxy XCover 7 Pro Receives Android 17 Update
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Samsung's toughest Galaxy phone just got Android 17 — here's how to check
Samsung is rolling out Android 17-based One UI 9 updates to Galaxy XCover 7 Pro devices. Carrier-locked models are receiving the firmware update G766USQUADZJ7, which includes interface improvements, enhanced privacy features, and app upgrades. The update adds customization options for Quick Settings, a location privacy indicator, and enhanced Samsung Notes and DeX features. A dedicated Warranty and care section is also added to Settings. The XCover 7 Pro, initially launched with One UI 7 on Android 15, now receives two major Android version upgrades. Samsung promises seven years of security updates for the device. Users can check for the update via Settings > Software update > Check for updates. Unlocked models will receive the update later, though the timeline is unspecified.

item.title: FAA to Replace Floppy Disk Systems in Air Traffic Control by 2028
item.description:
Source: Engadget, PCMag, Gizmodo Original headline: FAA Moves to Replace Floppy Disk Systems in Air Traffic Control by 2028
The FAA plans to replace its 1980s floppy disk-based air traffic control systems with a digital display system by 2028. The upgrade aims to improve efficiency, reduce maintenance costs, and enhance safety. Over 400 facilities currently use the outdated systems, which require manual disk replacements for data updates. The new Enterprise – Information Display System (E-IDS) will provide real-time alerts and updates. The first installations at Atlantic City, Nashville, Rochester, Atlanta, and Salt Lake City airports mark the start of a $292 million project awarded to Leidos. A 2024 GAO report criticized the reliance on obsolete technology, noting the cumbersome manual processes. The FAA faces challenges including project coordination issues and unreliable cost estimates, though the timeline was accelerated from 2034 to 2028. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy highlighted the rapid modernization efforts. The agency also struggles with staffing shortages as it seeks to hire more air traffic controllers amid a global talent gap.

item.title: Airbnb to Launch AI Travel Agent in 2027 with Custom Interface
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, Engadget, The Verge Original headline: Airbnb Set to Launch AI Travel Agent in 2027 with Custom Interface
Airbnb announced plans to launch an AI travel agent in early 2027, designed to offer a personalized interface for trip planning. CEO Brian Chesky criticized traditional chatbots, arguing they fail to capture the aspirational nature of travel, as 80% of users enjoy researching destinations. The AI agent will dynamically generate a custom interface using maps, photos, itineraries, and calendars, enabling real-time adjustments. It will integrate within the Airbnb app for direct bookings and expand to include services and experiences. Post-booking tasks like refunds and safety support will also be handled. The company cited 20 years of experience connecting hosts and guests to inform the agent’s design. TechCrunch noted previous hints about an AI agent, but Airbnb now specifies a 2027 rollout. The Verge described AI as 'the best thing to ever happen to Airbnb,' reshaping product development. Initial focus will be on core travel planning, with future expansions planned.

item.title: US Marines Deploy to Baltic Sea to Protect Undersea Cables from Russian Threat
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: US Marines head to the Baltic Sea to help NATO mission aimed at protecting European undersea cables from Russian interference
US Marines are deploying to the Baltic Sea to support NATO's Baltic Sentry mission, aimed at safeguarding undersea cables and pipelines from Russian interference. Around 48 Marines from the 2nd Reconnaissance Battalion and II Marine Expeditionary Force Information Group will join Finland's Coastal Brigade, marking the Corps' second Baltic Sentry deployment after a 2025 rotation. The team will use drones and sensors to provide real-time data to NATO's shared operational picture, operating under European allies' command. Maj. Gen. Daniel Shipley emphasized building a 'cohesive, lethal team' to deter hybrid threats, while Finnish Navy Chief Capt. Johan Tillander called the Marines' expertise 'perfectly suited' for the mission. Baltic Sentry was launched in 2025 following incidents like the 2024 severing of two fiber-optic cables and damage to the Estlink 2 power cable. Russian activity, including 500+ incidents of trawlers near UK-Europe cables and a rehearsed Arctic cable-cutting exercise, has heightened concerns. NATO and allies face escalating tensions with Moscow, including airspace violations and nuclear threats, while the Pentagon urges restraint in public rhetoric. The deployment reflects a low-profile, supportive role for US forces in the region.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Google Retires Firebase Studio, Pushes AI Tools
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Google is ditching Firebase Studio soon, and it wants you to use its newer AI tools instead
Google is retiring Firebase Studio, its online IDE for Firebase development, and encouraging developers to use its newer AI-focused tools. The company announced the sunset of Firebase Studio in March, with developers able to export data until March 22, 2027. The shift aims to streamline workflows and prioritize AI integration, as Google emphasizes its broader push for Gemini and AI-driven development. Firebase Studio, launched in 2025, included AI chatbot features but remained code-centric. Newer tools like Antigravity and Google AI Studio are designed for prompt-based development, with the latter offering a web-based interface for AI-assisted app creation. Antigravity, a desktop app, allows local code interaction and supports non-Google AI models. Developers can choose between these tools or alternatives like Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex, with cost and interface likely influencing migration decisions. Google framed the move as reducing redundancy since Firebase itself remains available through other IDEs.

item.title: Archaeologists Find 2,800-Year-Old Siberian Burial Mound With Cannabis
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Archaeologists Excavated a 2,800-Year-Old Siberian Burial Mound. It Was Packed With Cannabis
Archaeologists excavating a 2,800-year-old burial mound in Eastern Scythia, known as Tunnug 1, found cannabis residues and seeds, suggesting ancient use of the plant in funerary rites. Researchers from Germany’s Max Planck Institute and Russia’s Institute for the History of Material Culture analyzed hair samples and seeds, detecting 560 parts per billion of cannabinol. Over 1,500 cannabis seeds were recovered, comprising nearly all the plant material at the site. Radiocarbon dating of seeds from two coffins narrowed the cannabis use to the first decade of the 8th century BCE. The findings indicate the Scythian nomads were the first known to use cannabis for its psychoactive effects, though domesticated cannabis originated in East Asia 6,000 years ago. The site also included horse sacrifices, highlighting the cultural and ritual significance of the burial. Caspari noted the site underscores Inner Asia’s role in transcontinental cultural connections. The study, published in Science, links the Scythians to early horse cultures of Mongolia, suggesting east-to-west cultural exchanges.

item.title: Wonder Files for IPO as It Expands Food Tech Business
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Food delivery startup Wonder files for IPO as it explores its next big bite
Food delivery startup Wonder has confidentially filed for an initial public offering, marking a key step toward public trading. Founded in 2018 by Marc Lore, the company has expanded beyond traditional delivery apps to operate food hall-style locations offering meals from multiple restaurant brands. Wonder handles meal preparation, delivery, pickup, and dine-in services. The company raised over $650 million in a July funding round valued at $9 billion, with investors including Accel, GV, and ARK Invest. Wonder plans to open more than 100 locations in Texas by 2027 and has acquired Blue Apron, Grubhub, Tastemade, and Spyce, gaining automation technology. Its Wonder Create platform uses AI to design restaurant brands in under a minute. A $425 million partnership with DoorDash expands campus dining operations. Wonder faces competition from DoorDash and Uber Eats as it seeks to scale its food technology business.

item.title: Potassium-Enriched Salt Could Prevent 3 Million Annual Deaths, Study Finds
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: A Simple Kitchen Swap May Prevent Up to 3 Million Deaths a Year
Replacing standard table salt with potassium-enriched salt could prevent up to 3 million annual deaths from cardiovascular and chronic kidney diseases, according to a study by Australian and U.S. researchers. The authors modeled five scenarios, estimating that a full substitution of all table salt with a 25% potassium mix could prevent 2.96 million deaths and 10.17 million cardiovascular cases yearly. Even partial adoption, like switching salt used by people with hypertension, could prevent around 500,000 deaths annually. The World Health Organization endorsed potassium-enriched salt as a strategy to reduce sodium intake. However, the researchers caution that hyperkalemia risks exist, particularly for those with chronic kidney disease, though cardiovascular benefits may still outweigh these risks. The study highlights that potassium-enriched salt, which tastes similar to regular salt in most mixes, could be a practical tool to lower sodium consumption globally. Despite potential implementation challenges, the authors argue the health benefits of the switch are substantial.

item.title: iOS 27.3 Beta Adds Reachability for iPhone Duo One-Handed Use
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: iPhone Duo just got a new accessibility feature in iOS 27.3 beta
Apple released iOS 27.3 beta with a new accessibility feature for the iPhone Duo. The reachability function allows users to swipe outward from either edge of the exterior display, sliding content toward the thumb for one-handed use. This mirrors Apple's existing reachability feature introduced on the iPhone 6 in 2014, which typically pulled content downward on standard iPhones. The iPhone Duo's 5.4-inch OLED display benefits from this adjustment, enabling easier access to controls like the back button. Users can enable the feature in Settings under Accessibility > Touch. While reachability isn't new, its adaptation for the foldable's unique screen layout represents an incremental improvement for one-handed operation.

item.title: Lyft Launches $10/Month Subscription with DoorDash Benefits
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Lyft's new subscription bundles in DoorDash's DashPass for $10 per month
Lyft is replacing its Lyft Pink subscription with a new offering bundled into DoorDash's DashPass for $10 per month. Existing DashPass members can access Lyft Go at no extra cost. The annual plan costs $96, $3 less than Lyft Pink's previous price. Lyft Go members receive 8% back as credits per ride, up to $40 monthly, plus three relaxed cancellations. Credits can offset future rides or DoorDash orders. The plan also waives lost item return fees and matches charity donations. A lower-tier Lyft Go Core tier costs $5/month, offering 5% credits up to $20 and similar perks without DashPass. Lyft and DoorDash, which is acquiring Instacart for $17 billion, are expanding their partnership to let users browse DoorDash restaurants in the Lyft app. Lyft Go launches in the US with a one-month free trial, transitioning existing Lyft Pink subscribers at the same price. Uber's $10/month subscription service, Uber One, offers comparable benefits including ride credits and Eats discounts via Amazon Prime partnerships.

item.title: WhatsApp Adds Invite Links and Event Hub for Better Group Planning
item.description:
Source: PCMag, Engadget, Digital Trends Original headline: WhatsApp Expands Events Feature to Include Invite Links and Dedicated Management Hub
WhatsApp is updating its Events feature to include shareable invite links for non-users and a centralized management hub. The new tool allows users to create RSVP options like 'Going' or 'Not going' and personalize events with images, reminders, and location details. Non-WhatsApp users can view event info and respond without creating an account. Privacy settings hide the host's phone number from unknown guests and restrict address access until RSVP confirmation. The Events hub tracks past and upcoming plans, manages invitations, and syncs with calendars. The update aims to streamline group planning by reducing repetitive detail questions. WhatsApp is rolling out the feature gradually over weeks, expanding its ecosystem to include non-users after recent features like video calls and usernames. Digital Trends noted the shift from group chats to a dedicated space, while Engadget highlighted competition with platforms like Partiful. Hosts can now monitor all invites and scheduled calls from the hub.

item.title: Zelda remake leaks online days after Switch 2 launch
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Nintendo’s latest Zelda remake already circulating online as a Switch 2 ROM
Nintendo’s remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was leaked online the same day it launched on the Switch 2. Copies of the 1.0.0 release and its 1.1.1 update, totaling 23 GB, are circulating outside official channels. Physical copies had already appeared days before the release, with footage shared online by November 1. Emulators struggle to run the game, causing visual glitches or black screens. The game’s title ID is 0400486024DEC000, and files were extracted using tools like ns2jb and OunceCake. ns2jb, a tethered jailbreak developed by security researcher Sammy ‘pepsipu’ Hajhamid, allows homebrew execution and save file backups but requires reactivation after restarts. The exploit, which targets the Switch 2’s MMIO, has also been used on Deltarune and Mario Kart World. Nintendo has not commented on the leak but removed SmileBASIC 4 from the eShop after the exploit’s disclosure. The company previously targeted over 400 GitHub repos for cartridge-based backups.

item.title: WhatsApp Adds Photo Expansion Feature Using Meta AI for iOS Users
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: WhatsApp could soon let you expand photos with Meta AI on your iPhone
WhatsApp is adding a photo expansion feature for iOS users, similar to Apple's photo Extend tool. The update, available in beta for iPhone users, allows expanding photo edges using Meta AI to adjust aspect ratios or framing. Unlike Apple's feature, which requires Siri-compatible iPhones, WhatsApp's tool is accessible within the app without switching. Users can edit photos in chats, tap the expand tool, and preview AI-generated details before sending. The feature is tested with a small group of beta users, with Android users having had access longer. If unsatisfied, users can undo changes or retry the expansion. The option is hidden for square photos that already fit WhatsApp's supported frame. The update aims to streamline photo editing and sharing within the app.

item.title: Bose Recalls S1 Pro Battery Packs Over Fire Risks
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Bose recalls S1 Pro battery packs due to fire and overheating risks
Bose is recalling over 670,000 S1 Pro and S1 Pro+ battery packs in the US and Canada due to fire and overheating risks. The affected lithium-ion packs can overheat, ignite, or catch fire, causing property damage. Bose and the CPSC received seven reports of batteries melting, smoking, or catching fire, though no injuries have been reported. The recall includes packs sold from December 2017 to July 2026 at retailers like Best Buy, Amazon, and Walmart. Users must check their battery's 17-digit serial number against specific batches to determine if it's affected. Replacement batteries are available free on Bose's recall page. Affected users should stop using the packs immediately and avoid disposing of them in regular trash. The speakers themselves are safe to use on AC power while awaiting replacement.

item.title: Amazon and Uber Eats Offer Free Delivery for Prime Members
item.description:
Source: PCMag, Digital Trends Original headline: Amazon and Uber Eats Launch Delivery Partnership for Prime Members
Amazon and Uber Eats launched a partnership offering Prime members free delivery on orders of at least $25. Customers can order food from participating restaurants via Amazon’s website or app without needing an Uber Eats account. Delivery updates are sent via email and push notifications, with final confirmation from Uber Eats. The deal ends Amazon’s collaboration with Grubhub, as Prime members lose access to Grubhub+ benefits starting Thursday. Amazon Prime members can use saved payment methods and select nearby restaurants through the Amazon platform. The service is available in nearly 10,000 U.S. communities, including Atlanta, Los Angeles, and Houston, with access to hundreds of thousands of restaurants. Users can search for 'Uber Eats' on Amazon to grant access. The offer includes a $20 discount on the first two orders of $25 or more, valid through November 18. Prime Visa cardholders get 5% cashback on Uber Eats orders until December 5, 2026. Amazon claims the combined benefits could save members over $175 annually, enough to cover a Prime subscription. The partnership simplifies ordering by integrating Uber Eats within Amazon’s ecosystem, eliminating separate app logins. The $25 minimum may sometimes be more cost-effective than an Uber One subscription, though thresholds vary by restaurant and location. Amazon is sending targeted emails to promote the service.

item.title: Samsung's Android XR Glasses Begin Pre-Orders November 12
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Intelligent Eyewear: Samsung's Android XR glasses will start pre-orders in a week
Warby Parker announced pre-orders for Samsung's Android XR glasses, Intelligent Eyewear, will begin November 12. The company's CEO and co-CEO referred to the product as the 'first collection,' suggesting future collaborations with Samsung. Pre-orders will launch ahead of the holiday season, with delivery expected during the same period. Earlier rumors had speculated a mid-December release, but the Q3 earnings call confirmed an earlier timeline. Samsung's glasses, designed in partnership with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, use Qualcomm's Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 chip and are intended to work with Galaxy phones rather than replace them. The company aims to gauge consumer reception, with a potential focus on South Korea and the U.S. market. The product's design and functionality highlight Samsung's strategy to integrate AR technology into wearable devices.

item.title: Microsoft Updates Xbox PC App with Speed and Design Improvements
item.description:
Source: Engadget, Digital Trends, Gizmodo Original headline: Microsoft Enhances Xbox PC App with Speed and Design Overhaul
Microsoft is updating its Xbox PC app with performance and design improvements. The update, available to Xbox Insiders, reduces load times by up to 60 percent, with key sections loading 50 percent faster and in-app windows opening 65 percent quicker. The redesign streamlines navigation, adds unified search, and integrates social features into the main interface. The app now mirrors console aesthetics with dark/light modes, prominent game promotions, and redesigned game cards. Microsoft is extending these changes to Xbox cloud gaming apps for TVs and VR. A refreshed web version includes a Library tab, desktop mode, and high-contrast themes. While addressing performance issues, the app still faces competition from platforms like Steam. Microsoft plans to leverage Xbox Play Anywhere titles and explore new hardware, such as a standalone handheld device. The update’s success will depend on user feedback and its impact on PC gaming experiences.

item.title: Ex-Secret Service Agent Raises Second $250M Cybersecurity Fund
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: The ex-Secret Service agent who flipped a hacker is now raising a second $250M cybersecurity fund
Stephen Ward, a former Secret Service agent who once flipped a hacker into an informant, is raising a second $250 million cybersecurity fund. His firm, Brightmind Partners, previously led the Series A round of SGNL, which CrowdStrike acquired for $740 million in January. Ward’s approach to exits prioritizes selling early, a strategy shaped by his career in law enforcement and corporate cybersecurity. After leaving the Secret Service in 2001, he worked at TIAA and Home Depot before transitioning to venture capital. His first fund, launched in 2024, has made 14 investments, including the SGNL exit. Ward now leads Brightmind alone after co-founder Gur Talpaz left in April. He cites market trends, noting early-stage cybersecurity startups are raising more money than later-stage rivals for the first time in over a decade. Ward focuses on companies with strong exit potential, tracking acquisition patterns and buyer strategies. His second fund will allocate 20% to AI infrastructure and include Israeli-based startups. He emphasizes backing second-time founders who stay together, reflecting his own career path from military to cybersecurity to venture capital.

item.title: Dropbox Acquires Tigris Data for $350M to Boost AI Infrastructure
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Dropbox acquires Tigris Data for $350M to bolster its AI infrastructure
Dropbox acquired Tigris Data for $350 million to enhance its AI infrastructure. The deal, announced Thursday, is expected to close in Q4 2026 and will support the development of DBX Agent Cloud, a storage platform for businesses and developers building AI models. DBX Agent Cloud will initially offer object storage compatible with Amazon S3, enabling independent storage purchases. Dropbox also plans to expand the platform with features for handling documents, images, audio, and video, along with filesystem tools for AI agents. The company says the updated experience is available to 70,000 teams in the U.S., U.K., and Australia, with broader rollout planned for 2027. Tigris, founded by former Uber engineers, provides cloud storage technology that optimizes data access. The acquisition is Dropbox’s largest to date but follows prior AI-focused mergers, including Reclaim.ai and Mobius Labs. Tigris raised $25 million in Series A funding last year.

item.title: Google Adds 'Notify When Left Behind' Feature to Find Hub
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Google's Find Hub just got a feature that could save you from losing your wallet
Google is adding a "Notify when left behind" feature to Android's Find Hub for Bluetooth trackers. The update sends alerts when users move away from items with trackers, like wallets or keys. Apple has offered similar functionality through Find My for years, but this is the first time Android users gain the feature. To enable it, users open the Find Hub app, select a tracker, and toggle the setting. The feature currently works only with Bluetooth trackers, not other devices like headphones. Google revamped Find Hub last year, integrating tracking for devices, trackers, and people. The update aims to help users recover lost items, addressing a long-standing gap compared to Apple's existing capabilities. The change reflects ongoing improvements to Android's tracking ecosystem.

item.title: Sony Reissues 1979 Walkman Headphones with Modern Upgrades
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica, Engadget, Digital Trends, PCMag Original headline: Sony Revives 1979 Walkman Headphones with Modern Upgrades
Sony has reintroduced the MDR-3 series headphones, originally released in 1979 with the Walkman TPS-L2. The new MDR-3R model retains the retro design of the original MDR-3L2, featuring a gray plastic headband with metal sliders and orange ear cushions. Modern upgrades include a USB-C connector, built-in microphone, and inline volume knob. Two color options are available: standard blue/orange earpads at $60 and a limited-edition black/red version inspired by *Stranger Things* at $80. The headphones use 23mm drivers for warm, natural sound with minimal bass. While praised for lightweight build and open design, users note the short cable could be improved. The USB-C port ensures compatibility with modern devices but is incompatible with newer Walkman players. Sony’s retro revival aligns with nostalgia-driven tech trends, including cassette players and vintage phones. The MDR-3R is now available through major retailers.
item.source: Ars Technica, Engadget, Digital Trends, PCMag

item.title: Intel Nova Lake CPUs Face 5.1 GHz Thermal Limit Above 90°C
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Intel leaker claims Nova Lake desktop chips have 5.1 GHz clock limit beyond 90°C
Intel's upcoming Nova Lake desktop CPUs will have a 5.1 GHz clock limit when temperatures exceed 90°C, according to leaker Jaykihn. The limiter applies universally, meaning high clock rates require advanced cooling. Jaykihn notes the chips have a 100°C thermal limit (Tjmax), down from Arrow Lake's 105°C. The design resembles Intel's Thermal Velocity Boost, allowing higher speeds under optimal cooling. Nova Lake uses a 2nm TSMC N2P process for compute tiles, which may improve cooling efficiency despite lower power delivery. Users may need to undervolt to avoid thermal throttling, as the 5.1 GHz cap cannot be raised. AMD's Zen 6 Ryzen processors are rumored to exceed 6 GHz, potentially giving them a 20% clock advantage. Gaming performance could be 33% faster than Arrow Lake due to new architectures like APX cores and bLLC. The 52-core Nova Lake variant may debut next summer, but its performance impact remains uncertain. The Core Ultra 4000 series is expected to launch late 2024 or early 2025.

item.title: Axiom Math Verifies Stacks Project with AI Code
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Axiom Math wants to keep AI slop out of mathematics
Axiom Math has formally verified the Stacks Project, a massive open-source mathematics reference, using AI agents and Lean code. The project, initiated in 2005 by Johan de Jong, spans 7,654 pages of math from algebra to number theory. Axiom’s AI team translated this into 16 million lines of code, ensuring logical consistency across interconnected theorems. CEO Carina Hong emphasized the challenge of preserving mathematical coherence, noting that errors in foundational definitions could create paradoxes. The company trained its own AI models to grasp mathematical 'taste,' allowing agents to self-assign tasks and work in parallel. This effort fills a gap in formalized math, particularly in algebraic geometry, where prior work lacked verified foundations. Terence Tao noted that verified proofs enable future proofs to build on existing work. Axiom argues that verified mathematics provides a reusable substrate for AI agents, preventing 'slop' in software development. Hong challenges coding companies to adopt large-scale formalization, asserting it’s essential for future AI-driven innovation.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: ESP32 projects offer DIY solutions for car and driveway automation
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: 6 weekend ESP32 projects for your car and driveway (Nov 6 - 8)
Six ESP32-based projects offer DIY solutions for car and driveway automation. MiniSpeedCam uses a radar module and camera to detect speeding vehicles, uploading data to a server. Catchcam is a plug-and-play speed camera detector relying on OpenStreetMap data for over 66,000 camera locations. An OBD-II port reader project leverages ESP32 and Arduino libraries to access vehicle diagnostics. A parking sensor uses ultrasonic sensors and LED strips to guide reversing cars, with project author Alvise Susmel documenting the build. GPS speedometer projects include an ESP32 GPS-Speedo for RC cars and a Bluetooth-enabled TTGO Speedo. A smart garage door opener integrates with Home Assistant via ESPHome, while a 3D-printed parking guide aids vehicle alignment. Kits like Freematics ESP32 OBD and WiCAN meatPi simplify builds, with firmware and CAD files available for customization.

item.title: New York Times in Talks to Acquire Letterboxd for $330 Million
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, The Verge, Engadget Original headline: The New York Times Company in Talks to Acquire Letterboxd for $330 Million
The New York Times Company is in exclusive talks to acquire Letterboxd for $330 million, according to multiple reports. The deal would expand the Times’ digital ecosystem, integrating Letterboxd’s film-centric platform into its operations. Letterboxd, with 28 million users as of April 2023, targets younger audiences, offering free access with paid subscriptions for advanced features. Its projected 2023 earnings of $15 million contrast with the acquisition price. The Times explored other buyers, including A24 and Sony, but A24 was priced out. Letterboxd’s co-founders may retain leadership roles while reporting to a Times executive, with the platform likely remaining standalone. Integration of the Times’ ad technology into Letterboxd’s systems is planned. The Times, seeking to diversify revenue, aims to grow subscribers to 15 million by 2024. The acquisition would join previous deals like Wordle and The Athletic. The Times declined to comment, while Letterboxd and Tiny Ltd., its majority owner, did not immediately respond. The deal, if finalized, would mark a significant expansion for the Times’ digital strategy.

item.title: India aims to develop homegrown GPUs within 2 years
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: India targets creating homegrown GPUs within 2 years and plans to commercialize indigenous SHAKTI and VEGA processors
India aims to develop an indigenous GPU within 24 months under the India Semiconductor Mission 2.0, according to S.Krishnan, secretary of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. The initiative is part of a broader plan to build a domestic semiconductor ecosystem, including five layers for AI development: energy, accelerator chips, computing infrastructure, AI models, and applications. Companies like VVDN and C-DAC are already manufacturing servers and developing AI-supporting systems. Krishnan compares AI's potential to the Y2K IT boom, noting 2 million jobs may be displaced but 4 million new roles could emerge. Partnerships with ASML and Intel are advancing semiconductor manufacturing, though no GPU manufacturer has been named. SHAKTI and VEGA, RISC-V-based CPUs, are being commercialized for applications like autonomous robots and digital telescopes. Previous GPU efforts, including a 2019 software development kit and the 2024 Aries 3.0 board, focus on simpler tasks. The government’s DLI program supports projects in microcontrollers and smart devices. India’s semiconductor market, valued at $50 billion, is projected to reach $100 billion by 2030.

item.title: Two dead, five injured in Taiwan PCB factory explosion
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware
An explosion and fire at a Panasonic Industrial Devices Materials factory in Hsinchu, Taiwan, killed two people and injured five. The incident occurred at 2 am on Wednesday at a five-story facility producing printed circuit boards and semiconductor packaging materials. Initial reports indicated the use of flammable solvents like methanol and methyl ethyl ketone (MEK) as a possible cause, but the exact origin remains under investigation. Firefighters used heavy machinery to clear debris, recovering the two missing workers later. The facility, which passed a safety inspection in August, had 20+ staff on duty. The tragedy follows a similar explosion at an Intel facility in Israel last month. While the broader impact on the PCB supply chain remains unclear, the incident highlights ongoing safety concerns in the industry.

item.title: BioWare documentary set for release next year
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: A BioWare documentary is set to arrive next year
A documentary about BioWare's history is set for release next year. Filming began two years before Electronic Arts shut down the studio last month. Super Channel commissioned 'Massive Effect: The BioWare Story,' which will cover the studio's 31-year legacy, featuring founders Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk, and Augustine Yip, along with directors Casey Hudson and Jennifer Hale. Producer Shane Fennessey stated the film will document the studio's closure and its impact. Fans can contribute by sharing memories via a dedicated website. EA closed BioWare after its latest games underperformed, opting to invest in Star Wars Battlefront 3 instead of completing Mass Effect 5. The studio had around 50 employees and was developing a new Mass Effect game, whose trailer leaked before the shutdown. Bloomberg reported EA's decision to prioritize Battlefront 3 over the next Mass Effect title.

item.title: UK businesses face cyberattack risks from prioritizing recovery speed
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Businesses are putting themselves at risk of cyberattacks — by recovering too fast
UK businesses face cyberattack risks by prioritizing recovery speed over quality. Cohesity research shows 74% of firms focus on rapid recovery, with 70% failing to confirm attackers are fully removed from breached systems. Cyber resilience investments favor prevention over response, according to 76% of surveyed businesses. Leadership lacks clarity on IT readiness, with half of UK CEOs expecting operations to resume within 24 hours. Responsibility for post-attack restoration remains unclear, with no consensus on who should prioritize system recovery. The report advocates defining a Minimum Viable Company (MVC) to identify essential systems for operations. However, 41% of businesses lack an MVC definition, while only 17% have a documented one. "If you restore a system before verifying attacker access has genuinely been removed, you risk reinfecting yourself," said UK&I VP Fraser Hutchison. Organizations must clarify critical systems and assign responsibility for post-attack restoration.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Instagram Releases Edits App for Mac, Adds Advanced Editing Tools
item.description:
Source: Engadget, Digital Trends Original headline: Instagram Launches Edits App for Mac, Expands Editing Features
Instagram has released a macOS version of its Edits app, expanding video editing tools for creators. The desktop app includes a multi-track timeline, keyframes for transitions, precise audio waveforms, and color grading tools like color wheels and curves. Users can export 4K videos without watermarks and publish directly to Instagram. The app supports keyboard shortcuts, custom fonts, and pre-built templates, with AI-driven content optimization recommendations. It also allows importing custom LUTs and editing in multiple aspect ratios. Meta claims the desktop version is tailored for complex projects, leveraging larger screens and precision controls. CEO Mark Zuckerberg reported Edits has over 50 million active users. The app currently only works on Macs with Apple’s M-series chips and lacks Intel support. Meta plans to enable seamless switching between desktop and mobile versions for ongoing projects, enhancing cross-device integration.

item.title: Zipline's $21.5B Valuation Soars with Walmart Drone Expansion
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Zipline hits $21.5B valuation as Walmart expands bet on drone delivery
Zipline and Walmart expanded their drone delivery partnership, adding 300 new sites across the U.S. The companies, which had a deal since 2021, now operate 21 active sites. Zipline raised $1.5 billion in funding led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global, boosting its valuation to $21.5 billion. The funds will expand U.S. manufacturing and build a nationwide drone delivery network. Zipline, founded in 2014, initially focused on medical deliveries in Africa before entering the U.S. in 2020. Its 2022 FAA certification enabled long-range commercial deliveries, leading to partnerships like Uber. The company now delivers food, retail, and health products in Africa, the U.S., and Japan. Zipline’s delivery revenue share rose from 10.8% to 34.9% between March and October 2023, with plans to increase further.

item.title: Salon Closes After 31 Years as Digital Journalism Model Falters
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Salon is shutting down after 31 years
Salon, an online news magazine, is ceasing publication after 31 years. The company cited a 'no longer sustainable' publishing model, attributing the decision to shifting business realities in digital journalism, including challenges from Google Zero and AI tools. An unsigned post announced the closure, noting the legacy of its journalism and community. Salon's general manager, Amanda Wolfe, directed inquiries to the post. The editorial archive will remain accessible on Bluesky. Find.co, which acquired Salon in 2023, describes itself as a 'Performance Marketing Ecosystem transforming crypto marketing with performance and precision.' The closure marks the end of one of the first online-only news outlets.

item.title: Harbinger raises $240M as it expands into defense and hybrid vehicles
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Harbinger raises $240M after expanding into defense
Electric truck startup Harbinger raised $240 million in a Series D funding round as it expands into defense and other products. The round, co-led by Tiger Global, Capricorn’s technology impact fund, and Ridgeline, brings Harbinger’s total raised to over $650 million. FedEx, which previously led a $160 million Series C round, invested again and placed a $300 million order for 2,000 trucks. FedEx’s senior vice president of safety and transportation, Paul Melander, joined Harbinger’s board. The company, founded in 2022 by former Canoo and QuantumScape employees, has expanded beyond electric trucks to include battery storage, hybrid emergency vehicles, and a driverless military platform. It also acquired autonomy startup Phantom AI. Harbinger is reportedly considering an IPO, with Fidelity Management, a pre-IPO investor, participating in this round.

item.title: YouTuber Uses Airplane Sounds to Locate Individuals
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: A YouTuber Figured Out How to Find Almost Anyone Using Airplane Sounds
YouTuber Colsto demonstrated a method to determine a recording's location by analyzing airplane sounds. The technique uses Doppler effect patterns from aircraft to match audio with ADS-B flight data. By examining spectrograms of ambient sounds, Colsto identified Doppler curves from passing planes, narrowing down potential locations. He tested the method on a video of trees recorded on September 8, using ADS-B data to cross-reference flight paths and audio timestamps. The process involved filtering 70,000 candidate locations to a few dozen by analyzing subtle details in the Doppler curves, such as plane acceleration or altitude changes. Colsto eventually pinpointed the exact location using Google Street View. The method highlights how background noise in recordings can reveal unintended location data, raising privacy concerns. While the technique requires initial dataset narrowing, it shows how aircraft sounds can be used to geolocate audio with surprising accuracy.

item.title: Entrepreneur Solves Snoring Problem with Sleep App
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: The Snoring Problem That Launched a Tech Company: How One Entrepreneur Is Reinventing Sleep
Jules Goldberg, a British entrepreneur with no programming background, created SnoreLab, a popular sleep app, after his wife complained about his snoring. Frustrated by the lack of existing solutions, he taught himself Objective-C to develop the app, which records and analyzes snoring patterns. The app helps users track changes over time and test remedies like wedge pillows or CPAP machines. Goldberg emphasized that SnoreLab acts as a 'bathroom scale for snoring,' providing data to identify issues without curing them. He later expanded the technology to detect body movements using smartphone sound waves, leading to apps like Sleepwave, which tracks sleep without wearables. Goldberg, who built the business without investors, also holds a patent for using sound waves to address nasal congestion. His journey highlights self-taught entrepreneurship and the potential of smartphone tech for health monitoring, offering insights for sleep sufferers and aspiring innovators.

item.title: TikTok Launches Standalone Shop App in Multiple Regions
item.description:
Source: Engadget, TechCrunch
TikTok has launched a standalone Shop app for iOS and Android, now available in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and the Philippines. The app offers personalized product recommendations, shopping via livestreams and short-form videos, app-exclusive deals like free shipping, secure payment options, and order tracking. The move expands TikTok's e-commerce efforts, positioning it to compete with Amazon and Temu. TechCrunch noted the app was quietly rolled out in select markets, providing a dedicated space outside the main app to attract shoppers. The U.S. version of TikTok operates as a separate entity and has added features like voice comments and in-app travel booking. TikTok's broader strategy includes diversifying into games, restaurant guides, sports hubs, hotel booking, and microdramas. The launch marks a strategic shift in its rivalry with Amazon, which previously introduced a TikTok-like video feed called Inspire. The app's exclusive first-order benefits and incentivized shopping model highlight TikTok's focus on building a self-contained commerce ecosystem. The company has not commented on expansion plans or U.S. availability, leaving regional rollout timelines uncertain.

item.title: CleanMyMac Adds Gmail Inbox and Chrome Tab Management Tools
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: CleanMyMac can now clean up your Gmail inbox and tame your Chrome tabs
CleanMyMac now offers tools to manage Gmail inboxes and Chrome tabs. MacPaw’s Email Cleanup feature allows users to batch delete emails by sender, category, or attachment size, and unsubscribe from multiple mailing lists. It also shows storage recoverable from Google Drive and Photos. Deleted emails remain in Gmail’s Trash for 30 days, but drafts are permanently deleted. The tool uses Google sign-in without accessing email content. Browser Care, a Chrome extension, tracks tab memory usage, pauses slow tabs, and closes duplicate or long-idle tabs. Both features are free for existing CleanMyMac users. A March survey found 60% of Gmail users face inbox clutter, with nearly half still deleting emails manually. The tools aim to streamline email management and reduce browser resource consumption.

item.title: Samsung’s Galaxy Fit 4 Might Support Contactless Payments, Outperforming Fitbit Edge
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Samsung’s Next Fitness Tracker Might Have a Big Advantage Over the Fitbit Edge
Samsung’s Galaxy Fit 4 fitness tracker may support contactless payments via NFC, according to leaked app screenshots. The device’s companion app includes a 'Wallet' section for storing passes, tickets, and gym memberships, suggesting tap-to-pay functionality similar to Samsung’s smartphones. The tracker also features a speaker and haptic motor, upgrades from previous models. Unlike Google’s Fitbit Edge, which lacks NFC and contactless payment support, the Galaxy Fit 4 could offer a more convenient alternative for users avoiding smartwatches. Google cited low user adoption as reason for omitting NFC from the Fitbit Edge. Samsung’s new model appears to build on its Galaxy Fit 3 with enhanced features, positioning it as a more versatile option in the fitness tracker market.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Home Ethernet wiring can be repurposed with five tools for stable connections
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: Your home already has wired internet, you just need these 5 things to make it work
Your home may already have Ethernet wiring hidden in walls or coaxial cables. To leverage this, five methods can transform existing infrastructure into a wired network. First, an Ethernet cable tester can identify unused Cat5e/Cat6 cables in walls or telephone sockets. Second, replacing old RJ11 phone jacks with RJ45 keystone jacks can repurpose existing telephone wiring for Ethernet, requiring proper termination. Third, an unmanaged Ethernet switch can connect multiple wall ports if cables lead to a central wiring closet. Fourth, MoCA adapters can turn coaxial TV cables into a network by transmitting data over existing coax wiring. Lastly, powerline adapters use electrical outlets to create network connections, though performance depends on home wiring quality. These solutions, costing under $50, can eliminate Wi-Fi dead zones. Netgear's 8-port unmanaged switch is recommended for homes with existing Ethernet cables but no ports.

item.title: Morris Chang: Globalization and free trade are nearly dead
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Quote of the day by TSMC founder Morris Chang: 'Globalization is almost dead and free trade is almost dead"
Morris Chang, founder of TSMC, stated at the company's Arizona plant opening that globalization and free trade are 'almost dead.' TSMC produces 90% of the world's most advanced semiconductors and holds up to 70% market share in contract chip-making. Chang noted geopolitical tensions, especially between the U.S. and China, manufacturing repatriation, and bloc formation have reconfigured global supply chains. The 2020-2023 chip crisis, driven by lockdowns, geopolitical shifts, and just-in-time logistics failures, disrupted tech sectors. A new memory shortage, linked to AI data centers and demand for high-bandwidth memory, now affects consumer-grade products like DDR5 RAM and SSDs. Chang's remarks reflect a broader shift toward localized production and reduced reliance on global trade.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Nagare Labs’ Z2RAM aims to merge SRAM speed with DRAM density
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Gelsinger-backed Nagare Labs’ Z2RAM promises SRAM speed at DRAM density
Nagare Labs, a Georgia Tech spinout backed by Pat Gelsinger, claims its Z2RAM technology can deliver SRAM-speed memory at DRAM density by stacking layers directly on AI chips. The Gen 1 design projects 5x SRAM density, 14x DRAM speed, and 3x less read energy than SRAM. Founders Suman Datta and Shimeng Yu’s research shows retention of over 300 seconds at 85°C, though DRAM’s 95°C limit remains a hurdle. Z2RAM uses a two-transistor, single-shield cell design, avoiding capacitors and enabling non-destructive reads. The technology aims to address AI chips’ bandwidth needs by integrating memory on the die, bypassing interposers and bonds. However, challenges include heat management, fabrication scaling, and reliability concerns like single-electron effects. Nagare’s current prototypes are lab-based, with production targeting 2027-2030. The company seeks R&D fab partners and faces competition from existing solutions like HBM and AMD’s 3D V-Cache. While Z2RAM’s claims remain projections without full fabrication validation, it builds on prior capacitorless memory concepts like Innovative Silicon’s Z-RAM. Nagare’s board includes Gelsinger, who previously led Intel’s shift away from Optane memory.
